items.text: Recall: $\mathbf{Cat}_D$
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(C,C')\ \subset\ \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C,C')\ \ \text{full: functors commuting with limits of type } D',D''
$D$: sets $D'$, $D''$ and exactness properties $(E_\alpha,\Sigma_\alpha)$: every $\varphi\colon E_\alpha\to C$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$ inverts $\Sigma_\alpha$.
Assumption 1: for every category $I$, $C\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(I,C)$ on $\mathbf{Cat}_D$ is 2-representable, by $\widetilde I\in\mathbf{Cat}_D$.
Assumption 2: for $C\in\mathbf{Cat}_D$, $\Sigma\subset\operatorname{Fl}(C)$,
R\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(C,R;\Sigma)\ \ \text{2-represented by } C[\Sigma^{-1}]\in\mathbf{Cat}_D
2-limits in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$
2-inverse limit of $(C_i)$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$:
\operatorname{Hom}_D(C,\mathbb L)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \mathbb L_i\,\operatorname{Hom}_D(C,C_i)
$\mathbb L$ = 2-inverse limit in $\mathbf{Cat}$ (Cartesian sections of the fibred category over $I$); limits of type $D'$, $D''$ computed componentwise, exactness properties inherited.
2-direct limit of $(C_i)$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$:
\operatorname{Hom}_D(C,C')\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \mathbb L_i\,\operatorname{Hom}_D(C_i,C')
In $\mathbf{Cat}$: $L=F[\mathrm{Cart}^{-1}]$ ($F\to I$ the fibred category, invert the Cartesian arrows).

Then pass to $\widetilde L$ and invert $\Sigma$ = the arrows $u_i(\varprojlim x_\alpha)\to\varprojlim u_i(x_\alpha)$, $\varinjlim u_i(x_\alpha)\to u_i(\varinjlim x_\alpha)$ coming from limits of type $D',D''$ in the $C_i$:
\varinjlim{}^{\,2}_{\mathbf{Cat}_D}C_i\ =\ \widetilde L[\Sigma^{-1}]
Examples of $D$
(1) Finite inverse limits; left exact functors.
(2) Arbitrary inverse limits ($C\hookrightarrow\widehat C$: a structure on $X$ = a structure on the functor it represents).
(3) Preordered categories (every morphism is a monomorphism): ordered sets with finite lower bounds, increasing maps.
(4) Additive (semi-additive) categories: initial = final object, $X\sqcup Y\to X\times Y$ an isomorphism; additive functors.
(5) Abelian categories, exact functors; the universal abelian category on one object is $\widetilde I$, $I$ = one point.
(6) Abelian categories with exact filtering direct limits.
(7) Finite inverse and finite direct limits (pretopoi, coherent topoi).
(8) Topoi: finite inverse limits and arbitrary direct limits; the 2-category of topoi.
(9) Essential topoi: add (a) arbitrary products of epimorphisms are epimorphisms; (b) products commute with sums.
\text{essential topos with generators}\ =\ \widehat C
